When Savoy College opened he continued as a student there, and since his arrival in Texas he has turned his attention almost exclusively farming, and is active at the age of seventy-seven years.

Professor E. H. Pritchett, the oldest of his parental family of five children, received his education at public schools in Fannin County. When Savoy College opened he continued as a student there and then entered the junior class of Alabama Polytechnic Institute in January of 1879, graduating in 1880 with the B. E. degree.

From correspondence in the Bonham Daily Favorite, it is learned that after the destruction of Savoy College, Professor Pritchett then took up the study of law and was admitted to the bar of Texas. He made a career as a civil engineer and lawyer, however, fitted him so well for his public life about him in Texas that he continued to occupy that position. As found in the county Abstract of Fannie County, Mr. Pritchett served for many years as steward and Sunday School superintendent at Bonham, and was a member of the Methodist Episcopal Church.

Mr. Pritchett was married January 16, 1885, to Miss (Augustine) Evans, a prominent family of Bonham, Texas, now, et al., deceased, who was employed in the land department. They had no children to add to this family sketch.
